existing_interactions.hypothesis: BTTS-no is dominated by 0-0, 1-0 and 0-1 cells so rho changes the price more than lambda for low-scoring pairs.
Hot-keeper form regresses; the shrunk keeper effect, not recent clean sheets, should enter clean-sheet markets.
Missing first-choice defenders matter more for the team that already concedes openly; effect is convex in lambda.

btts_and_clean_sheet.existing_mechanism: BTTS requires each team to score at least once, so it is controlled by the lower-lambda team's probability of scoring and by the dependence between scoring events. Keeper quality, defensive absences and tempo shift clean-sheet probability; the dependence parameter shifts the joint zero-zero and one-nil cells. First-half variant is lower-count and more dependent on the half split.

First-half draw probability is the intersection of dependence and low lambdas, so the two must be jointly modelled.
Second-half goal multipliers depend on half-time score and on bench strength after substitutions.

Draws are very likely in first-half result markets, so dependence and draw propensity dominate. Second-half markets need conditional modelling from half-time state and substitution dynamics.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: Consistency between hazard integral and the 0-0 cell is a check on the goal model.
High-press sides score earlier so hazards peak early rather than being proportional to full-match lambda.
Dead-ball and penalty events provide step increments in hazard not captured by open-play xG.

first_to_score_event.existing_mechanism: First-to-score is a race between two inhomogeneous Poisson processes with a null outcome for 0-0. existing_interactions.hypothesis: Integrating lambda uncertainty fattens tails; ignoring it under-prices big margins and high scores.
Fitted rho and lambdas must be consistent with AH and total lines; residual score cells are the exact-score signal.
Late game chasing makes heavy favourites' margin distribution depend on bench depth and substitutions.

handicap_and_exact_score.existing_mechanism: Handicap and exact-score markets are functionals of the full joint goal distribution: handicap prices need the goal-difference distribution including margins, and exact score prices need every cell. They are sensitive to the distribution tail, dependence parameters and lambda errors. Push/split rules for integer and quarter lines matter. The edge, if any, is more likely in consistency across rungs than in a lineup effect.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: Lineup shortfalls reduce the attack/defence components separately, so a missing striker mainly lowers own goals and a missing centre-back mainly raises opponent goals.
Dead-rubber matches raise rotation, which changes both expected strength and the draw share.
Evenly matched teams at a strong-HFA venue convert draw mass to home wins; in neutral venues the draw share is higher.
Price comparison needs favourite-longshot and draw-bias correction to avoid false edges on the draw rung.

match_result_3way.existing_mechanism: A joint goal model converts opponent-adjusted attack/defence strengths and home advantage into the 3-way probability vector. The draw is the hard part: it depends on closeness, total expected goals, Dixon-Coles dependence and team draw propensity. Incremental information arrives through confirmed lineups, rotation and stakes, so the price must be updated for team news that is stale in earlier quotes. A two-way winner wording changes how draws are treated (void/advancement/extra time) and must be parsed.

existing_inputs.label: Shots and shots-on-target for/against
existing_inputs.why: Team shots and SOT for and against set the volume to be shared.

existing_inputs.label: Player shot and shot-on-target share of team volume
existing_inputs.why: Player share by role converts team volume to player volume.

existing_inputs.label: Confirmed lineups timestamped
existing_inputs.why: Confirmed lineup fixes who plays and in which role.

existing_inputs.label: Expected minutes and rotation risk for a player
existing_inputs.why: Expected minutes and substitution risk scale every shot and save count.

existing_inputs.label: Expected shots-on-target faced by the goalkeeper
existing_inputs.why: Expected SOT faced is the keeper-saves volume.

existing_inputs.label: Goalkeeper quality and PSxG-GA
existing_inputs.why: Keeper quality (PSxG minus goals allowed) shrunk toward average.

existing_inputs.label: Tempo, pressing intensity, possession style
existing_inputs.why: Pressing and tempo change shot volume.

existing_inputs.label: Game state effects, red cards, substitutions
existing_inputs.why: Trailing teams shoot more; leading teams concede more shots.

existing_inputs.label: Opponent shots and chances conceded by zone and position
existing_inputs.why: Opponent block and zone profile changes shot conversion to SOT.

existing_inputs.label: Formation/tactical system and expected pressing matchup
existing_inputs.why: Formation changes who takes shots.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: Shot volume is convex in expected deficit: heavy underdogs concede many shots while taking few, changing both player and keeper counts.
Keeper saves depend on volume times shrunk skill; volume dominates unless skill is extreme.
A teammate's absence raises shot share in a position-specific way.

unreg:player_shots_saves_props.existing_mechanism: Shot counts are team shot volume times the player's share times minutes, shaped by game state (trailing teams shoot more) and the opponent's block and press profile. Goalkeeper saves are the opponent's shots on target times the keeper's save probability, which is noisy and must be shrunk. Both are over-dispersed counts and depend on the confirmed lineup.
unreg:player_shots_saves_props.label: Soccer player shots, shots on target and goalkeeper saves
unreg:player_shots_saves_props.target: A player's shot or shot-on-target count, or a goalkeeper's saves, relative to a threshold.
